extracted.intended_audience: USPTO examiners and patent owners/attorneys practicing in ex parte reexamination proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards for handling papers, petitions, amendments, final actions, and patentability review conferences in ex parte reexamination proceedings before the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service of submission and certificate of service timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Service of the submission must be made, and a certificate of service provided to the Office within a shortened statutory period of ONE MONTH or THIRTY DAYS, whichever is longer, from the mailing date of the letter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If service is not timely made, the submission may be denied consideration. Examiner Note: paragraph used where a submission to the Office was not served as required in a third party requester reexamination proceeding. Use bracketed insertion of --patent owner-- or --third party requester-- as appropriate. Cover sheet for mailing notice is form PTOL-473.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of failure to serve
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure of a party to serve the submission in response to the notice may result in refusal of consideration or termination of prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (A) For a patent owner statement or third party reply the submission may be refused consideration and not addressed in the reexamination proceeding other than to inform parties of the lack of consideration. (B) For a patent owner response to an Office action, the response may be refused consideration; where consideration is refused, prosecution may be terminated under 37 CFR 1.550(d) unless the owner has otherwise completely responded. See MPEP §§ 2220, 2249, 2251, 2266.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of inappropriate or untimely filed papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain types of correspondence will not be considered or acknowledged unless timely received; upon receipt, Office must decide action based on paper type and timeliness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inappropriate submissions will be returned or forwarded to one of three files: Reexamination File (paper or IFW history), Patent File (paper or IFW history), or Storage File (paper). Papers returned from a Technology Center must be accompanied by a letter indicating signature/approval of the TC Director. Returning inappropriate submissions reduces scanning into the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director approval required to return certain papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Some papers require approval of the Director of the USPTO or TC Director to return.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a paper is to be returned based on listed criteria and is not accompanied by a petition under 37 CFR 1.182 or 1.183, the TC Director will return the paper. Where such a petition has been filed, the reexamination proceeding should be forwarded to the Office of Patent Legal Administration for decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Premature responses by patent owner (returned)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the patent owner is NOT the requester, any response or amendment filed by owner prior to an order to reexamine is premature and will be returned and will not be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited authorities: § 1.530(a), § 1.540, § 1.550(g).

rubrics_metrics.name: Papers submitted on behalf of a third party (returned)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission filed on behalf of a third party will be returned and will not be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where third party paper is submitted as part of a patent owner response, see MPEP §§ 2254 and 2266.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unsigned papers (owner or requester)
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers filed which are unsigned (or signed by less than all owners, or without attorney of record) will not be considered or will be located in the reexamination file as defective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filed by Owner: unsigned or signed by less than all owners (no attorney of record or acting in representative capacity). Filed by Requester: unsigned papers will not be considered. Authorities: §§ 1.33, 1.248, § 1.535.

rubrics_metrics.name: No proof of service (defect)
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers filed without proof of service on the required party may be denied consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Papers filed by patent owner in which no proof of service on requester is included (and where proof is required) may be denied consideration. Similarly, papers filed by requester without proof of service on owner may be denied. Authorities: § 1.33, § 1.248, § 1.510(b)(5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Untimely papers (not considered)
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers filed after the period set for response will not be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where owner has filed a paper which was filed after the period set for response, the paper will not be considered. Authorities: § 1.530(b), § 1.540.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party submissions after order placed in Storage File
rubrics_metrics.description: Third-party submissions based solely on prior art patents or publications filed after the date of the order to reexamine are not entered into the patent file but are delayed until reexamination proceedings have concluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 2206. Proper timely filed citations by third parties (filed prior to the order) are placed in the reexamination file. Authority: § 1.501; citation: § 1.550(h).

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to revive reexamination/proceeding — revival fees and statutory basis
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions for revival of unintentionally abandoned applications, delayed fee payments, or unintentionally delayed responses in reexamination require revival fees and must meet statutory provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revival fees: e.g., $1,500 for many petitions (unless filed under sections 133 or 151 then $500). Authorities: 35 U.S.C. 41; 35 U.S.C. 133; 37 CFR 1.137.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition based on unavoidable delay (37 CFR 1.137(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition to revive based on unavoidable delay must show the delay was unavoidable with adequate supporting details and evidence, and be accompanied by required filings and fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must provide adequate showing of the cause of unavoidable delay including details and evidence; accompanied by petition fee per 37 CFR 1.17(l) and a proposed response to continue prosecution (unless previously filed). See MPEP § 711.03(c), part III for detailed discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition based on unintentional delay (37 CFR 1.137(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition to revive based on unintentional delay must include a verified statement that the delay was unintentional, a proposed response, and the petition fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must include verified statement that entire delay was unintentional, proposed response to continue prosecution (unless previously filed), and the petition fee per 37 CFR 1.17(m). Office may require additional information where question exists whether delay was unintentional. Applies to ex parte reexamination by 35 U.S.C. 41(a)(7) and AIPA section 4605.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewed petition / reconsideration timing and form
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for reconsideration of a decision dismissing or denying a petition under 37 CFR 1.137(a) or (b) must be filed within one month of the decision and use specified cover letter titles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cover letter should be entitled “Renewed Petition under 37 CFR 1.137(a)” or “Renewed Petition under 37 CFR 1.137(b)” as appropriate. Extensions of time may be requested only under 37 CFR 1.550(c); 1.136 extensions not available in reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconsideration requires patent owner response to Office action
rubrics_metrics.description: To be entitled to reconsideration, the patent owner must respond to the Office action (37 CFR 1.111(b)); responses may be with or without amendment until action is final.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any amendment after the second Office action, which will normally be final, must ordinarily be restricted to the rejection or to the objection or requirement made. See 37 CFR 1.112 and MPEP § 2271.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clerical handling and entry of amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: The reexamination clerk handles initial clerical processing; amendments complying with 37 CFR 1.530(d)-(j) will be entered for reexamination in the reexamination file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments entered for reexamination even if they do not have legal effect until certificate issued. “New matter” amendments to disclosure must be canceled and claims containing new matter rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112. New matter to drawings ordinarily not entered. Amendments that enlarge claim scope will be entered but appropriate claims will be rejected under 35 U.S.C. 305. For merged reissue-reexamination, see MPEP §§ 2283, 2285.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final action — development of clear issue before final
rubrics_metrics.description: Before issuing a final action, a clear issue should be developed between the examiner and patent owner, with the examiner providing information and references twice to define the Office’s position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial decision ordering reexamination will identify new questions of patentability raised by prior art. First Office action should reflect consideration of arguments/amendments in request and owner's statement and replies, and should fully apply all relevant grounds of rejection to the claims. The second Office action following decision ordering reexamination is intended to be final in accordance with MPEP § 706.07(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Final rejection content — grounds and appealability
rubrics_metrics.description: In making a final rejection, all outstanding grounds of rejection of record should be carefully reviewed and any ground relied on should be reiterated and clearly developed so patent owner may judge advisability of an appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a single previous Office action contains a complete statement of a ground, the final rejection may refer to that statement but should include a rebuttal of any arguments raised in the patent owner’s response. Final rejection must be developed to the extent that patent owner can judge appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability review conference required stages
rubrics_metrics.description: A patentability review conference must be convened (A) just prior to issuing a final rejection and (B) just prior to issuing a Notice of Intent to Issue Ex Parte Reexamination Certificate (NIRC), with specified exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions: when NIRC follows and is consistent with a Board or court decision on merits, or where NIRC is consequence of patent owner failure to respond resulting in cancellation of all claims. Conference reviews examiner’s preliminary decision to reject/allow claims prior to issuance; if conference confirms examiner, Office action is issued and conferees initial action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make-up and selection of patentability review conference members
rubrics_metrics.description: Conference will consist of three members, one may be the SPE; examiner in charge plus two examiner-conferees selected by the SPE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conferees will be primary examiners or examiners knowledgeable in the technology and/or experienced in reexamination practice. Majority of those present should be examiners not involved in original examination/issuance. An original examiner should be chosen only if most knowledgeable or other specific justifiable reason exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability review conference process and outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner informs SPE of intent to issue final rejection or NIRC; SPE convenes conference; if conference confirms examiner decision, Office action issued with signatures/initials; if not, examiner issues appropriate Office action reflecting conference decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If examiner in charge disagrees with conference decision, SPE will generally assign proceeding to another examiner, preferably one of the conferees. When conference results in final rejection or NIRC, two conferees initial as 'conferee' to indicate participation; both initial even if one dissented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose / scope of patentability review conference
rubrics_metrics.description: Each conference provides forum to consider all issues of patentability and procedural issues affecting patentability, to ensure comprehensive discussion and findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review by more than one primary examiner diminishes perception of disproportionate influence and helps detect issues the examiner in charge might have missed. Conference provides comprehensive discussion of, and finding for, each issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences and remedy for failure to hold conference
rubrics_metrics.description: If examiner issues final rejection or NIRC without holding required conference, parties must promptly file a paper alerting the Office; failure to hold conference is not alone grounds for vacating decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any challenge must be made within two months of the Office action issued or it will not be considered. Whether to convene a conference to reconsider will be addressed case-by-case; mere failure to hold conference does not restart reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 22.09/22.10 — final action notification and shortened statutory period
rubrics_metrics.description: Final rejection letter should conclude with form paragraph indicating action is final and specifying shortened statutory period for response (normally two months, or one month in court-stayed litigation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions of time under 37 CFR 1.136(a) do not apply; extensions provided under 37 CFR 1.550(c) must be filed on or before due date with petition fee per 1.17(g) and granted only for sufficient cause. Filing a timely first response to final rejection is construed as including a request to extend the shortened statutory period by one month; maximum statutory period for response cannot exceed six months from mailing date of final action. For ¶22.10, insert filing date of amendment in bracket 1 and appropriate period for response in bracket 2; final Office action must be signed by a primary examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Art submitted by patent owner during prosecution may allow finalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Where art is submitted as a prior art citation under 37 CFR 1.501 and/or 1.555 and not accompanied by a statement similar to 1.97(e), the examiner may use the art and make the next Office action final provided no other new ground of rejection is introduced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 706.07(a). IDS filed in a reexamination is construed as a prior art citation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signatory authority for final Office actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Final Office actions in reexamination proceedings must be signed by a primary examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies to all Office correspondence on the merits in a reexamination proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: After-final practice — limits on further prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: Prosecution before the examiner in a reexamination proceeding is intended to be concluded with the final action; patent owner has no right to unrestricted further prosecution after a proper final rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consideration of amendments after final rejection is governed by strict standards of 37 CFR 1.116 (and after appeal by 37 CFR 41.33). Identify and develop all issues prior to final Office action, including evidence under 37 CFR 1.131 and 1.132. Patents undergoing reexamination cannot become abandoned or be refiled; cancellation in a certificate is final.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time for response to final rejection and automatic extension rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Statutory period for response to a final rejection in a reexamination proceeding is normally two months; filing a timely first response automatically extends the period by one month (subject to limits).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Automatic one-month extension applies if the response is the first after the final rejection and a notice of appeal has not been filed. Advisory Office action PTOL-467 informs owner of the automatic extension. The response period may not be extended past six months from the date of the final rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner action on amendments filed after final rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent owner cannot as a matter of right amend finally rejected claims, add new claims after final rejection, or reinstate canceled claims; amendments after final are subject to 37 CFR 1.116 standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An amendment filed after final and prior to appeal brief requires a showing under 37 CFR 1.116(b) and will be evaluated by the examiner except where amendment merely cancels claims, adopts examiner suggestions, removes issues for appeal, or requires only cursory review. The first proposed amendment after final will be given sufficient consideration; if not entered in its entirety, examiner will explain reasons and identify any new issues requiring further search. Second or subsequent amendments after final considered only to the extent they remove issues for appeal or place a claim in obvious patentable condition.
